description: Solar leads in Faridabad: a 30-day playbook for installers covering Meta, Google, Maps and referrals, with sector targeting and filters that cut wasted calls.
headline: Solar leads in Faridabad: a 30-day playbook for installers
card_text: A week-by-week plan for Faridabad installers: sector-level targeting, Google and Meta setup, Maps, sector referrals and the filters that stop shared-roof and bulk-connection leads wasting your team's time.
intro:
Getting solar leads in Faridabad is not hard. Getting leads your team can actually install is. Faridabad is a long city stretched along the Mathura Road corridor, from the older sectors and NIT in the north to Ballabgarh and the newer Greater Faridabad sectors across the canal. A lead from the wrong end of town, a builder floor with a disputed roof or a high-rise flat on a bulk connection can look exactly like a good lead in your ad report.

This post is a 30-day playbook for Faridabad installers who want a steady flow of rooftop solar leads from Meta, Google, Maps and referrals. It covers what to set up each week, how to target by sector, and which Faridabad-specific filters to build in from day one. If you want the bigger picture on running separate residential and commercial campaigns here, read our solar marketing guide for Faridabad alongside this one.

sections.h2: Before you start: map Faridabad the way your survey team sees it
sections.html:
Most installers set their ad location to "Faridabad" with a radius and hope for the best. That wastes money in a city this long. Spend an hour with your survey and installation team and split the city into zones you can serve in one trip:

ZoneExamplesWhat the roofs usually look like
Older sectorsSectors 14, 15, 16, 21, 28, 37 and nearbyIndependent houses, owner controls the roof, high summer bills
NIT and Old FaridabadNIT 1–5 and older coloniesDense plots and builder floors, roof rights often shared
Ballabgarh sideBallabgarh town and surrounding sectorsMix of houses and small commercial buildings
Greater FaridabadSectors 75–89 along the Neharpar sideMostly high-rise societies, plus some plotted pockets

Write down which zones you will run ads in, which pincodes belong to each, and how far your team is willing to travel for a survey. Every later decision, from ad targeting to the first question on the call, comes from this map.

sections.h2: Week 1: fix the base that every solar lead in Faridabad checks
sections.html:
A Faridabad homeowner who sees your ad will usually search your name, check your Google rating and ask a neighbour before taking a survey. Fix these before you spend on ads:

  1. Google Business Profile. Correct category, real address, service areas that match your zone map, opening hours, and photos of systems you installed in Faridabad. Add a short post about the subsidy process every couple of weeks.
  2. A Faridabad landing page. One page that names the sectors you serve, shows local installations, explains the DHBVN net-metering steps in plain Hindi and English, and has a click-to-call button plus a WhatsApp button.
  3. A lead sheet or CRM. Columns for date, source, zone, own house or rented, roof type, monthly bill, called, survey booked and installed. Without this you will never know which channel is working.
  4. A response owner. One person who calls every new lead within minutes during working hours and sends a WhatsApp message if the call isn't picked up.

Ask your last 10–15 installed customers for a Google review this week too. A short WhatsApp message with your review link, sent the day after commissioning, works better than asking months later.

sections.h2: Week 2: launch Google Search for buyers who are already looking
sections.html:
Google Search brings fewer solar leads than Meta, but they tend to be people who have already decided to look at solar. In Faridabad, searches mix English, Hindi and Hinglish, so build ad groups around how people actually type:

  • "solar panel installation in Faridabad", "rooftop solar Faridabad", "solar company near me"
  • "solar subsidy Faridabad", "PM Surya Ghar Faridabad", "DHBVN net metering"
  • "solar panel lagwana hai", "ghar ke liye solar" style Hindi and Hinglish phrases

Target your chosen pincodes rather than a big radius, and set the location option to people in your area, not people interested in it. Add negative keywords early: jobs, training, course, dealership, wholesale, price list PDF, and the names of towns you don't serve. Send all clicks to the Faridabad landing page, not your homepage. Our Google Ads guide for solar companies covers keyword match types and call tracking in more detail.

sections.h2: Week 3: add Meta lead ads with Faridabad-specific filters
sections.html:
Meta (Facebook and Instagram) is where most solar leads in Faridabad will come from by volume, because it reaches homeowners who haven't searched yet. Volume is also why it needs the strongest filters. Build the instant form around the problems that are common in this city:

  1. Do you own the house, or is it rented? Removes tenants straight away.
  2. Which type of home? Independent house, builder floor, or flat in a society. A flat owner in a Greater Faridabad society usually can't get an individual net meter if the society has a single-point bulk connection, so route these leads to an RWA pitch instead of a home survey.
  3. For builder floors: is the roof yours to use? In NIT and older colonies the roof is often shared. Asking now saves a wasted survey trip.
  4. Monthly electricity bill range. Helps you size the system and prioritise calls.
  5. Pincode or sector. Lets you reject leads outside your zones before calling.

Use creatives shot on Faridabad roofs, with the sector named in the caption where the customer agrees. A 20-second video of a finished system and the owner's new bill usually beats a stock image of a villa. The full setup is in our Facebook ads for solar installers guide.

sections.h2: Week 4: start the referral loop inside sectors
sections.html:
Faridabad's older sectors are close-knit. Once one house on a street installs solar, the neighbours notice the panels and ask about the bill. Turn that into a system:

  • After commissioning, ask the customer for a review and for the names of two neighbours or relatives who might be interested.
  • Offer a simple, honest reward, such as a free annual cleaning visit, rather than cash promises you may not keep.
  • Run a small Meta campaign targeted to the same sector with the installation photo, so neighbours see a roof they recognise.
  • Keep a sector-wise list of installations. When a new lead comes in, mention a nearby system they can look at.

Referral leads are usually the cheapest and fastest to close, but they only grow if you ask every time. Track them as their own source in your sheet.

sections.h2: Get the DHBVN and subsidy facts right on every call
sections.html:
Faridabad buyers compare quotes, and one wrong fact on a call can cost you the order. Brief your team on these and check them before each campaign:

  • DISCOM: Faridabad is served by Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN). The net-metering application, feasibility check and bi-directional meter go through DHBVN. Installers commonly quote around a month or more from application to meter, so give a range, not a promise.
  • Sanctioned load: the system size is generally limited by the connection's sanctioned load, and DHBVN checks transformer capacity. Ask for a recent bill early so you can check this.
  • Central subsidy: under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, eligible households currently get central financial assistance of ₹30,000 per kW for the first 2 kW and ₹18,000 for the third kW, capped at ₹78,000 for 3 kW and above. Confirm current amounts on pmsuryaghar.gov.in.
  • State support: sources disagree on whether Haryana currently offers an extra top-up and for whom. Don't put a state figure in an ad unless you have the current order from HAREDA or DHBVN in hand.

For wording that keeps subsidy claims accurate in ads, see our guide to PM Surya Ghar subsidy ads.

sections.h2: How to judge your Faridabad lead sources after 30 days
sections.html:
At the end of the month, don't compare channels on cost per lead alone. Compare them on what matters to an installer:

MetricWhy it matters
Cost per leadThe starting point, but cheap leads can be the most expensive to process
Contact rateShare of leads your team actually spoke to
Qualified rateOwners with a usable roof inside your zones
Cost per survey bookedThe number that tells you which channel to scale
Survey to order rateShows whether your pitch, pricing and proof are working

Break each number down by zone too. You may find, for example, that one area brings cheap leads that rarely book surveys while another brings fewer but better ones. Move budget towards the zones and channels with the lowest cost per survey, and keep testing new creatives every couple of weeks. For context, our own rooftop solar campaigns have delivered qualified enquiries at ₹60–80 each, but every market and offer is different, so judge your numbers against your own close rate rather than a benchmark.

faqs: How can I get solar leads in Faridabad?

Start with a well-kept Google Business Profile and a Faridabad landing page, then run Google Search ads for high-intent searches and Meta lead ads for volume, both targeted to the sectors and pincodes your team can reach. Add a referral routine after every installation.
Which areas of Faridabad are best for rooftop solar leads?

Independent houses in the older sectors usually make the easiest residential leads because the owner controls the roof. Builder floors in NIT need a roof-rights check, and flats in Greater Faridabad societies are often better approached through the RWA.
Can a flat owner in a Greater Faridabad society get rooftop solar?

If the society has a single-point bulk connection, the RWA is the DHBVN consumer, so individual flat owners usually can't get their own net meter. Common-area solar for the society is the more practical pitch.
How long does DHBVN net metering take in Faridabad?

It varies with the application and feasibility check. Installers commonly quote around a month or more from application to meter installation, so give buyers a range and check the current process on the DHBVN and PM Surya Ghar portals.
